name: 24AA025UID I2C EEPROM with a serial number
description: Microchip 24AA025UID 2-Kbit (256 x 8) serial EEPROM on I2C: the lower half writable in 16-byte pages with a self-timed write cycle (no ACK while it runs), the upper half write-protected with the manufacturer and device codes and a 32-bit serial number.

pins.name: A0
pins.doc: Chip address bit 0: high adds it to 0x50 (tie low when unused)

pins.name: A1
pins.doc: Chip address bit 1: high adds it to 0x50 (tie low when unused)

pins.name: A2
pins.doc: Chip address bit 2: high adds it to 0x50 (tie low when unused)

twc.doc: Write cycle time: a real part took between 3.10 and 4.03 ms (sigrok's captures); the datasheet's maximum is 5 ms, for the worst case

serial.doc: The 32-bit serial number at FCh-FFh, programmed at the factory (default: the part sigrok's captures were taken from, 000FAC0Fh)

contents.doc: The lower half as a programmer left it, up to 128 bytes in hexadecimal from 00h; empty is erased (FFh), as shipped

outputs.name: writes
outputs.doc: Bytes committed to the lower half

functional.claims: Address 0x50 + A2..A0, one word-address byte, byte and page writes committed at STOP with the 16-byte page wrap (later bytes overwrite earlier ones), no write after a repeated START, an address alone moves the pointer, sequential reads rolling over at FFh, no ACK during the write cycle (ACK polling), the upper half write-protected (writes acknowledged, nothing changed) with 29h, 41h and the serial number at FAh-FFh.
omissions: contents are not kept between sessions
the bus speed limit (400 kHz): faster clocks are decoded too
whether a write to the protected half starts a write cycle (the captures do not show it): the model runs one
the write cycle time is fixed (twc); the real one varies with the part, supply and temperature
